question: What is the main use of a word processor in the clinic?

options.A: To calculate monthly hospital drug inventories automatically
options.B: To store secure backup images of ultrasound scans
options.C: To track real-time changes in a patient's blood pressure
options.D: To create, edit, format, and print text documents

explanation: Word processors are software tools used specifically for handling text-based paperwork like reports and care plans. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is moving from paper registers to digital typing helpful for healthcare records?

options.A: It guarantees that patient files can never be accessed by unauthorized persons
options.B: It completely removes the need for any physical patient folders
options.C: It allows computers to diagnose minor pregnancy complications automatically
options.D: It ensures clinical records are legible, secure, and easily updated

explanation: Digital text avoids poor handwriting issues and allows staff to modify or review records clearly and efficiently. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which command do you use when saving a new document for the first time to choose its folder and name?
explanation: Save As prompts the user to select a destination folder and assign a specific title to a new document. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between the Save command and the Save As command?

options.A: Save As permanently deletes older versions, while Save keeps all historical drafts
options.B: Save compresses the file size, while Save As expands it for editing
options.C: Save As allows you to create a new file name or location, while Save just updates the current file
options.D: Save requires an internet connection, while Save As works offline only

explanation: Using Save simply overwrites the current open file with your latest edits, whereas Save As lets you save a copy in a new file or destination. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which tool helps you duplicate a clinic instruction without retyping it?
explanation: Copying creates a duplicate of the selected text, allowing you to paste it elsewhere without removing the original text. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h3)

question: A midwife spelled a patient's surname wrong twenty times in a report. Which feature fixes this the fastest?
explanation: Find and Replace scans the entire document for the incorrect spelling and updates every instance automatically in seconds. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which font style is best to use for formal clinical reports?
explanation: Calibri and other clean, standard fonts ensure maximum readability and maintain a professional appearance in official documents. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is it better to use line spacing of 1.15 or 1.5 in professional documents instead of single spacing?

options.A: It is legally mandated for all international health ministries
options.B: It prevents unauthorized persons from printing the document
options.C: It automatically corrects spelling mistakes in the body text
options.D: It gives readers more visual breathing room and space for notes

explanation: Increased line spacing prevents text from looking cramped and makes dense clinical information much easier to read. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h4)

question: What are the individual rectangular boxes formed by intersecting rows and columns in a table called?
explanation: Cells are the individual blocks where text or numbers are typed inside a structured table. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why are tables useful when preparing a midwife shift duty roster?

options.A: They organize names, dates, and shifts into clean, structured categories
options.B: They convert text automatically into graphical pie charts
options.C: They automatically email the roster to all staff members on duty
options.D: They prevent any changes from being made to the schedule

explanation: Tables use rows and columns to align related pieces of information neatly, making schedules easy to interpret at a glance. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h5)

question: What feature should a student midwife always check before printing a multipage clinical report?
explanation: Print Preview shows how the document will look on paper, helping catch layout errors before wasting ink and paper. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using only the built-in spelling and grammar checker for medical documents?

options.A: It only functions when the computer is connected to a printer
options.B: It changes the font style of the entire document without warning
options.C: It permanently deletes words it does not recognize
options.D: It may flag correct specialized medical terms as errors

explanation: Standard dictionary software is built for general language and often fails to recognize uncommon clinical terms and drug names. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T1#BMP123_U3_T1_h6)
